### Axioms as directions, in one animation

<p align="center"><img src="{{fig:axiom_arrows_qwen3.5-2b.gif}}" alt="Pairs of group-like structures that differ in one axiom, drawn as 3-D arrows that slide to one common origin; Qwen3.5-2B left, its random-init twin right" width="720"></p>

- **What you see:** the 13 group-like structures (magma, unital magma, quasigroup, loop, semigroup, monoid, group, and the commutative versions of all but the unital magma) in the top-3 principal components of Qwen3.5-2B (left) and of its random-init twin (right), at the preregistered layer. One axiom at a time, every pair of structures that differ only in that axiom becomes an arrow, for example monoid → commutative monoid and group → abelian group for commutativity. The arrows then slide to one common origin, so you can see whether they point the same way.
- **What to notice:** in the trained model the commutativity arrows form one bundle. Their offset consistency, the mean cosine between the {{num:mvp.lattice.qwen3.5-2b.group_like.offsets.commutative.n_pairs}} difference vectors in the full residual stream, is {{num:mvp.lattice.qwen3.5-2b.group_like.offsets.commutative.consistency:.2f}}. The twin's is {{num:mvp.lattice.qwen3.5-2b__random.group_like.offsets.commutative.consistency:.2f}}, and random pairs of the same structures exceed {{num:mvp.lattice.qwen3.5-2b.group_like.offsets.commutative.null95:.2f}} only 5% of the time. Associativity behaves the same way ({{num:mvp.lattice.qwen3.5-2b.group_like.offsets.associative.consistency:.2f}}, twin {{num:mvp.lattice.qwen3.5-2b__random.group_like.offsets.associative.consistency:.2f}}). Identity ({{num:mvp.lattice.qwen3.5-2b.group_like.offsets.identity.consistency:.2f}}) and divisibility ({{num:mvp.lattice.qwen3.5-2b.group_like.offsets.divisible.consistency:.2f}}) form looser bundles.
- **Caveat:** three principal components can hide or exaggerate parallelism, so the statistic is computed in the full space, never from this picture. In Qwen3.5-2B only associativity and commutativity survive Holm correction; identity and divisibility are significant before correction only (the scorecard below has every model). Step-by-step static explainer: [`axioms_explainer_qwen3.5-2b.png`](reports/figures/axioms_explainer_qwen3.5-2b.png). [Interactive: how the test works](https://burnycoder.github.io/geometry-of-representations-of-mathematics-in-llms/#fig-axiom-how), and [the lattice in 3-D](https://burnycoder.github.io/geometry-of-representations-of-mathematics-in-llms/#fig-lattice).

## Highlights

*Every "n of 5" count below is computed from the results files (fact placeholders in `reports/readme_top_template.md`).*

**Positive results.** Each model is compared with its random-init twin: the same architecture and tokenizer, with no learning.
- **Axioms act as directions.** In the lattice magma → semigroup → monoid → group → abelian group, "add associativity" and "add commutativity" are consistent vectors: same-axiom differences are parallel. Associativity survives Holm correction in {{fact:axiom_holm.associative}}, commutativity in {{fact:axiom_holm.commutative}}. The twins show much weaker offsets; in {{fact:twins_any_offset}}, one or two axioms still pass the random-pair test before correction, from word form alone. "Add identity" and "add divisibility" point the same way but more weakly: identity is Holm-significant in {{fact:axiom_holm.identity}}, divisibility in {{fact:axiom_holm.divisible}}.
  - *How the test works:* for each axiom, take every pair of structures that differ only in that axiom, subtract their representations, and measure how parallel these difference vectors are (mean pairwise cosine in the full residual stream) against random pairs of the same structures. Step-by-step figure: [`axioms_explainer_qwen3.5-2b.png`]({{fig:axioms_explainer_qwen3.5-2b}}).
- **Lie groups sit between "group" and "smooth manifold".** The analogies topological group − group ≈ topological space − set, and Lie group − topological group ≈ smooth manifold − topological space, hold in {{fact:parallelograms}} (exploratory). The twins rank "group" first or second among the neighbours of "Lie group" because of the shared word, and except for Gemma's twin they place "smooth manifold" far away.
- **Math fields form a map.** Field centroids from {{num:mvp.map_fields.qwen3.5-2b.math_primary.n_fields}} fields correlate with how often mathematicians cross-list papers between those fields on arXiv. This was the primary preregistered hypothesis (H-A1). It holds beyond the twin in {{fact:field_map_beats_twin}} (Qwen3.5-2B/0.8B, Qwen2.5-1.5B, Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B, Gemma-4-E2B), and every random-init twin is near zero or below. In Qwen3.5-2B, the only model run against baselines, the map is stronger than in fastText word vectors and about as strong as in a dedicated text-embedding model ([Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B)).
- **Class-inclusion chains are ordered**, e.g. rng ⊃ ring ⊃ commutative ring ⊃ integral domain ⊃ … ⊃ field ⊃ algebraically closed field, and T0 ⊃ T1 ⊃ Hausdorff ⊃ … ⊃ Hilbert space. The full preregistered test (Robinson score and leave-one-out order, Holm-corrected, above the twin) holds for the space chain in {{fact:chain_ordered.space_chain}} and for the ring chain in {{fact:chain_ordered.ring_chain}}.
- **Concrete ↔ abstract is the top principal axis** of math-concept space in Qwen3.5-2B; pure ↔ applied is the second. Abstraction is rated by three LLM judges from other model families.

**Negative and null results:**
- **Angles are not a circle.** In every trained model, "330 degrees" is farther from "0 degrees" than neighbouring angles are from each other (closure ratio {{fact:angles_closure_range}}), and the angles' geometry tracks the bare numerals. This falsifies one of our preregistered predictions. Numbers lie on a generalized helix whose periodic parts need not show in the first two principal components ([Kantamneni & Tegmark 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.00873)), so we also looked in all 10 planes of the top 5 components. That test was post-hoc, but specified in writing and committed before it ran ([addendum](reports/prereg_addendum_3d.md)). No model has a significant closed cycle there either.
- **The map is not a clean hierarchy (H-A2).** Under the preregistered measure (cophenetic correlation with a five-branch super-tree), the trained models beat shuffled trees in {{fact:beats_shuffled_trees}}, but beat their random-init twins in none. By cophenetic correlation, no model is more tree-like than a Gaussian cloud with the same spectrum; relative Gromov δ, a second tree measure, does call {{fact:gaussian_more_treelike.delta_rel}} more tree-like than that cloud.
- **Over a trillion tokens of math pretraining did not sharpen the map.** Qwen2.5-Math vs its base ([Qwen2.5-Math report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.12122)) shows no detectable difference (H-A3).
- **Field clustering is not special to mathematics.** Biology, chemistry, geology and astronomy topics cluster by field more strongly than most random sets of four math fields, in {{fact:control_beats_most_math_subsets}}. This is a post-hoc clustering test; the control fields have no arXiv map.
- **The causal test was inconclusive.** The ring chain failed the accuracy gate. For the space chain, noise in the chain subspace hurt accuracy only slightly more than random-subspace noise, and only at the larger noise scales.
- **The positive control (days and months as circles) failed our preregistered full-space criterion, and replicates only partly with post-hoc tests.**
  - In the top-2 principal-component plane, where [Engels et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.14860) show their raw-activation circles, days go round in perfect order in {{fact:top2_cycle_perfect.days}} and months in {{fact:top2_cycle_perfect.months}}. But that score also rewards an open arc.
  - Counting only loops that close in their plane (the same addendum), days close in the top-2 plane in {{fact:closes_top2.days}}. Months close in a lower plane (PC2–PC3 or PC4–PC5; p < .05 each, unadjusted) in {{fact:closes_lower_plane.months}}.
  - A closed months loop also appears in {{fact:twin_closes.months}}, so this test is not fully specific. All outcomes are reported.

**Methods finding.** Before touching LLM data, we simulated partial regression on distance matrices. When the nuisance matrix is only a proxy of a confounder, it rejects true nulls far too often. That is why the field-map tests (H-A1 to H-A3) are paired contrasts against the random-init twin with concept-bootstrap CIs, and why every other test is also compared with the twin.
